title: UGS - Universal Gap Schema v1
description: The join between a job posting (UJD) and a career record (URS). Neither side is redefined here: this document says only which requirements the record satisfies, by what evidence, how short it falls, and what would close the difference. See references/ugs-spec.md.

Id.description: Stable identifier, prefixed by kind: asm_, gas_, sur_, srf_, qst_, mth_, cmp_. Same shape as a URS and a UJD id, so ids from all three documents cross-reference without a translation table. Ids borrowed from the other two documents keep their own prefixes: req_ and grp_ come from UJD, everything else from URS.

ForeignId.description: An id belonging to one of the two subject documents, not minted here. Never rewritten - a gap document that renames the things it points at cannot be checked against them.

Pointer.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the subject document, e.g. /skills/0 or /engagements/1/achievements/0. Carried alongside the id, never instead of it: the id survives reordering and the pointer locates the node without a scan.

Confidence.description: How much this assertion should be trusted. Never a match score and never aggregated into one - it qualifies the assertion, it does not rank the candidate.

Provenance.description: On every assertion, as in URS and UJD. The status vocabulary is identical in all three so `confirmed` means the same thing everywhere; the source vocabulary differs because a gap assertion is derived from two documents rather than read from one.

status.description: `confirmed` means a human or a rule established it from both documents. `inferred` means a model concluded it. `needs-verification` is the honest default for anything a model produced that a person has not yet checked.

kind.description: `both-documents` is the only kind that can support a satisfaction verdict. `posting-only` and `record-only` mark an assertion made with one side missing - which is how an absent skill and an unread resume section come to look identical if this is collapsed.

method.description: The Method that produced this assertion. Required at conformance Level 2: extraction reliability varies by an order of magnitude between methods, so an assertion whose method is unknown cannot be weighed.

stage.description: Which pipeline stage produced this. Recognition errors propagate into disambiguation, so a wrong verdict traceable only to 'the pipeline' cannot be localised or fixed.

then.description: An inferred source cannot yield a confirmed status. Laundering a guess into a fact is the failure this document exists to prevent, and it is the rule URS and UJD already enforce.

vocabularies.description: MUST name the same files both subject documents name. Two documents scored against different capability vocabularies are not comparable, and the mismatch is silent - a synonym scores zero and reads as absent evidence.

purpose.description: What this document was produced for. Deliberately has no value for screening, ranking or selecting candidates: UGS models one record against one posting for the person described by that record, and nothing here is fit for filtering applicants.

Subjects.description: The two documents this gap analysis joins. Both are pinned: a gap document is only meaningful against the exact versions it was computed from, and postings are edited and taken down.

ref.description: Path or URI of the UJD document.

ujd.description: The ujd version string of that document.

checksum.description: Of the UJD document as read. A gap verdict recomputed against an edited posting is a different verdict.

ref.description: Path or URI of the URS document.

view.description: The URS view this analysis was run against, when it was run against a rendered view rather than the whole record. Required to interpret `surface` at all: a keyword is only missing from something.

EligibilityGate.description: Hard filters, evaluated and reported separately from every score. UJD keeps work authorization, clearance and applicant location out of `requirements` so no skills overlap can offset a visa bar; UGS keeps the same separation on the answer side. A failing gate is never a low score - it is a different kind of answer.

verdict.description: `indeterminate` when the posting is silent or the record does not say. It is not a pass.

Evidence.description: One pointer from a requirement to the part of the career record that bears on it. A requirement may have several; `covers` is how two half-matching engagements jointly satisfy one demand without either being overstated.

record_id.description: The URS entity id: skill_, ach_, prj_, eng_, cred_, edu_, nar_ or pos_.

relation.description: `direct` is the same thing the posting asked for. `transferable` is a different thing that does the same job and must be argued. `adjacent` is nearby and does not substitute. `asserted-only` is a record claim with no backing evidence of its own - it looks identical to `direct` in a keyword match and is the single most dangerous thing to score, which is why it is named.

covers.description: How much of this one requirement this one piece of evidence accounts for. Values across a requirement's evidence may sum past 1; overlap is real and clamping it hides it.

span.description: The verbatim text from the record this rests on. Retained so the verdict stays checkable against the source: roughly 1% of real resumes carry hidden instructions aimed at automated readers and most avoid obvious instruction keywords, so a decision that cannot be re-read against the original text cannot be audited.

recency.description: When this evidence was last true. Drawn from URS last_used or the engagement period.

Shortfall.description: How far short, on one named axis. Typed rather than free text so a scorer can read it and a human can argue with it. Several may apply to one requirement: eight years demanded and five held, last used three years ago, is two shortfalls and not one.

required.description: What the posting demands on this axis, in the posting's own terms.

evidenced.description: What the record shows on this axis. `null` means nothing in the record speaks to it, which is different from zero.

delta.description: Signed distance, negative when short. Only meaningful for ordered dimensions.

unknown.description: The required value could not be determined from the posting. This is a real and common state, not a failure to try: trained human annotators agree only moderately on the qualification level a vacancy demands, so a required level asserted with false precision is worse than one marked unknown.

Counterfactual.description: What would close this gap. A gap with no counterfactual is a verdict; a gap with one is something the person can act on, and it is the unit published explainable matching systems actually surface.

kind.description: `surface-existing` means the record already holds it and the rendered resume does not show it - the cheapest fix there is. `cannot-close` is honest and belongs here: a licence nobody can obtain in the time available is not an action item.

closes.description: Assessment ids this one action would resolve. One answer often closes several.

Assessment.description: One requirement, judged. This is the join, and it is the only place a satisfaction claim may live. The requirement is referenced, never restated: UJD owns necessity, weight, vocabulary and raw text, and a copy of them here would drift.

requirement.description: The UJD requirement id (req_). Every requirement in the posting SHOULD have exactly one assessment; a requirement with none is unexamined, which is not the same as satisfied.

label.description: The posting's own phrasing, denormalised for readability only. Never matched on, never scored - the vocabulary term in UJD is the matchable value.

verdict.description: `unsatisfied` means the record shows the person does not have it. `unevidenced` means the record claims it with nothing behind it - a claim that survives a keyword scan and collapses under one interview question. `stale` means held, but not recently enough for what the posting asked. `indeterminate` means the comparison could not be made, and it is a legitimate answer that must not be silently rendered as `unsatisfied`.

question.description: The Question that would resolve this, when a person has to answer it.

group.description: Mirrors UJD requirement.group. Present so a reader can see this requirement is one arm of a choice rather than a standing demand - a partial here may cost nothing if another branch holds.

then.description: A satisfaction claim without a pointer to what satisfies it is an assertion. This is the rule the whole document is built to enforce.
Partial on no named axis is a hedge, not a finding.
An unevidenced claim is exactly the thing a person must confirm, correct or cut. Recording one without asking leaves it in the resume.

GroupAssessment.description: A UJD RequirementGroup, judged as a group. 'A degree AND six years, OR a postgraduate qualification' is one demand with two branches, and it must be answered as one: flattening it into three independent requirements scores a master's holder as missing two must-haves, and flattening it into a single `any` over all three lets the bare degree satisfy it. Both are wrong, which is why UJD models the group and UGS answers it here rather than in `assessments`.

satisfy.description: Denormalised from UJD so this record reads standalone. It MUST equal the value in the referenced group.

branches.description: One entry per direct member, in the group's own order. A member that is itself a group is answered by its own GroupAssessment and referenced here - nesting is preserved, never expanded.

member.description: A req_ or grp_ id from the group's members.

assessment.description: The Assessment (for a req_ member) or GroupAssessment (for a grp_ member) that carries the working.

distance.description: How far this branch is from satisfied, on a scale the document defines and states in Score.components[].method. 0 is satisfied. Comparable only between branches of the same group - it is a local ordering, not a score.

closest_branch.description: Which branch is nearest to satisfied, when the group is not satisfied. This is the actionable half of the answer: 'you are one year short on the degree-and-experience arm' is advice, 'you fail the qualification clause' is not.

then.description: An unsatisfied group that cannot say which branch was closest has thrown away the only part of the answer the person can act on.

Surplus.description: What the candidate has that the posting never asked for. The inverse of a gap and deliberately a first-class array: a matcher that only counts deficits cannot see the thing that makes an application interesting, and no surveyed standard models this at all.

value.description: The vocabulary term, when it resolves to one.

relevance.description: `reframes` is the rare one worth the space: something the posting did not ask for that changes what the application is about. `incidental` is honest and most surplus is that.

SurfaceGap.description: Held in the record, absent from what gets sent. A distinct failure from not having the thing, with a distinct and much cheaper fix, and the two are indistinguishable to any reader looking only at the rendered document. Only meaningful when subjects.record.view names what was rendered.

term.description: The term the posting uses. Literal - ATS matching does not stem or expand.

record_ids.description: Where it lives in the record. If this is empty it is not a surface gap, it is an absence.

aliases_available.description: From URS skill.aliases. The variant the posting used may already be recorded and simply not rendered.

Question.description: Written ready to ask, because a queue of fifteen gets abandoned and one gets answered. The ordering is the one the gaps mode already prescribes.

text.description: The question as it would be said aloud, including the quoted claim it challenges. A prompt that still needs rewriting before it can be asked is a note, not a question.

priority.description: In order. `blocking` stops a resume going out at all. `inferred-claim` is content nobody has confirmed. `missing-metric` is a true claim with no number. `unexplored` is territory never discussed.

about.description: Assessment, GroupAssessment, Surplus or SurfaceGap ids this would resolve.

quoted_claim.description: The exact record text being challenged, so the person is shown what they are being asked about rather than a paraphrase of it.

expected.description: What kind of answer closes it. `confirm-correct-or-cut` is the inferred-claim contract: all three outcomes are fine and leaving it as-is is not.

resolution.description: `unavailable` is a real outcome - a metric nobody can reconstruct. It resolves the question and should soften or cut the claim, not leave it pending forever.

ScoreComponent.description: One axis of fit, on its own, with its own working shown.

axis.description: The axis this measures, e.g. capability, technology, domain, seniority. Free text because the vocabularies are project-defined, but it MUST name something a reader can locate in meta.vocabularies or in the UJD matching model.

value.description: The component's own value, in its own units.

of.description: The assessments this component was computed from. A component that cannot name them cannot be checked.

explanation.description: One sentence a person could argue with.

Score.description: Decomposed, always. Audited whole-document similarity screening - one opaque number per candidate - favoured White-associated names in 85.1% of tested cases, disadvantaged Black male candidates in up to 100%, and reversed its preference when names were swapped for equally frequent ones from the model's own training corpus. The number was never about the requirements. A per-requirement decomposition is not a fairness guarantee, but it is the minimum that makes a disputed outcome traceable to something a person can point at.

aggregate.description: Optional, and constrained on purpose. An aggregate may exist only if it can say exactly how it was computed and from which components. An aggregate that cannot is the failure mode this schema is built against, so the schema refuses to hold one.

formula.description: Stated plainly, e.g. 'sum(weight x normalized) over components, capped at 1'. Prose is acceptable; absence is not.

excludes_implicit.description: Whether requirements the posting never stated were left out. UJD names them `implicit` precisely so a scorer can drop them in one predicate; saying which way it went is part of showing the working.

eligibility_excluded.description: Eligibility is never a score component. The field exists so the guarantee is visible in the document rather than only in the prose, and it can only hold one value.

Method.description: How assertions were produced, recorded once and referenced. Method is not a detail: on the same vacancy-linking task a supervised model reached F1 54.3 where a general-purpose LLM reached 0.22, and the best reported accuracy for linking vacancy text to a skills taxonomy was under 0.40. An assertion whose method is unknown cannot be weighed, and one whose method is assumed will be over-weighed.

model_version.description: Recorded because the same nominal method changes behaviour between versions, and a verdict that cannot name the version cannot be reproduced.

taxonomy_version.description: Vintage. A code without its scheme version is undecodable - the same rule UJD applies to occupation codes.

reliability.description: What is known about how well this method performs, including that nothing is known. A method with no reliability note is not disqualified; one with a fabricated one is.

Review.description: Whether a person has looked. Kept as a field rather than left implicit because 'a human reviewed it' is the claim most often made about automated assessment and least often recorded, and because the difference between a draft and a checked document is invisible once both are JSON.

state.description: `not-reviewed` is the honest default for anything a pipeline just produced.

reviewer.description: A role or a handle. Not a demographic, never a candidate attribute.

overrides.description: Where a person disagreed with the pipeline. Kept, rather than applied silently, because a document that quietly absorbs its corrections cannot show which verdicts a machine produced and which a person did.
